video.title: Billy Quit his Job to Start an AI App Agency: Here's How

summary: Billy Howell, a self-taught vibe coder and former defense contractor, explains how he runs an AI app agency (Stupid Simple Apps) with a team of four, building small custom internal apps for business owners using Replit, v0, Cursor and similar tools. He describes landing his first app job on Upwork by building a demo and undercutting a no-code stack, and gives detailed Upwork tips (Looms, connects, client vetting). He advises against starting with consumer apps, shares side-project ideas (recipe generator, plant time-lapse), and discusses shiny-object syndrome and building in public for inbound. Key takeaway: sell niche B2B custom apps to paying clients first, using fast AI-built demos and relationship-based sales.

speakers.name: Billy Howell
speakers.description: Vibe coder, founder of Stupid Simple Apps agency, ex-defense contractor and ex-marketing agency owner

ideas.name: Stupid Simple Apps (AI-coded custom app agency)
ideas.one_liner: Agency building small custom internal apps for business owners and startups using Replit, v0, Cursor and similar AI coding tools, sourced via Upwork and personal brand.
ideas.business_model: One-off build fees plus small monthly hosting/maintenance fee; B2B project work
ideas.customer: Small business owners and startups needing niche internal tools (data entry, dashboards, CRMs)
ideas.problem: No-code stacks like Airtable plus software are costly and over-complex; off-the-shelf SaaS does too much or lacks niche features
ideas.offer: Custom, simple one-to-few-feature app built quickly with AI coding tools, with demo shown before or at the sale

pricing.model: Build fee plus monthly run fee

price_points.label: Hosting/running the garage coaching data-entry app

pricing.notes: Build fee for the first app not stated. Compared against about $250/month for the no-code stack.

acquisition_channels.details: Upwork proposals with Loom videos, boosted with connects (about $0.15 each, $3-4 per proposal); first app client found there.

quote.text: I'm on Upwork sitting at my desk and I'm looking at this and I'm like okay like bluecollar guy
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

acquisition_channels.details: Posted a viral video about selling an app; records himself building client/personal projects in Replit for Twitter and YouTube; Replit's CEO retweeted one.
Inbound from Twitter/YouTube following, with an agency landing page and paid Calendly to capture it.
Relationship-based B2B selling; sells to existing relationships and community contacts.

ideas.delivery: Billy and a team of four build apps with Replit/v0/Cursor; last 10% (security review, refactor, Stripe, production readiness) is slow and done via back-and-forth with the AI agent or outsourced developers.
unit_economics_claims: Garage app: client saved about $250/month no-code stack cost by paying $50/month
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Billy says you could go from nothing to freelancer/agency in 2-3 weeks

acquisition.how: Upwork proposals and content can be drafted with AI but personal Looms, timing and relationship selling need a human.

onboarding.how: Scoping calls and demo creation with v0/Replit are quick but need human conversation.

delivery.how: AI coding agents build most of the app; human review needed for the last 10%, security and edge cases.

billing.how: Stripe subscriptions and invoices are automatable.

support.how: Bugs, changes and custom tweaks need human triage with agent assistance.

uk_applicability.notes: Upwork and AI coding tools work in the UK; UK clients can be targeted; VAT and GDPR for client data apply.

risks: Hiring overseas devs for bounties can fail
Agency can hit bandwidth limits and a deliverable treadmill
Security and quality of AI-written code

tactics.name: Demo-first selling with AI prototyping
steps: Read the client's Upwork post
Build a clickable prototype in v0 or Replit within minutes
Record a Loom comparing the custom app to the no-code alternative with costs
Offer a low monthly run fee below the alternative's cost

quote.text: get good at making like a something that's like a clickable interface that brings their idea to life and if you can do that in five minutes I think it's definitely worth doing it to make the sale
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

tactics.name: Upwork profile and proposal playbook
steps: Use a professional shoulders-up headshot
List a major metro as location instead of an obscure suburb
Check new job posts regularly because timing matters
Record a Loom showing your face with a tight proposal
Show past work and reassure on location/trust
Spend connects to rank at top every time

tactics.name: Vet Upwork clients
steps: Check total spend (at least a couple thousand dollars)
Check star rating and hiring history
Check past hourly rates paid
Read the post tone for defensive or tire-kicker signals

tactics.name: Small troubleshooting jobs to enter
steps: Search for broken Make.com or GoHighLevel automations
Take small-scope jobs big agencies skip
Convert one-off audits into recurring consulting calls

tactics.name: Research demand using Upwork from both sides
steps: List industries and contacts you know
Search workflow keywords on Upwork client and freelancer sides
See what packages freelancers sell
Pitch the validated service directly to your contacts

tactics.name: Build in public and capture inbound
steps: Record yourself building client or personal projects
Post to Twitter and YouTube consistently
Set up an agency landing page and paid Calendly in advance
Share value openly

tactics.name: Finish the last 10% with AI
steps: Pull code into Cursor or Windsurf
Ask the agent to review each page for security
Refactor step by step
Keep scope small so there are few edge cases

warnings.warning: Don't start with direct-to-consumer apps as your first app; it is a money pit without paying customers to guide features.

quote.text: I don't start with direct to consumer if it's your first app. Like, do not. It is a money pit, a pit of despair.
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

warnings.warning: The last 10% of an AI-built app takes longer than the first 90%, and even good devs prefer rebuilding from scratch.

quote.text: It takes longer than the first 90%.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Upwork applications are flooded with bots; clients may filter AI-looking proposals.
Standing up an agency quickly can exhaust bandwidth; hire early or face a deliverable treadmill.

quote.text: you're going to run out of bandwidth. So you need to have the foresight and be good enough at hiring to hire early or you're going to be on like a deliverable treadmill.
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

warnings.warning: Offshore hires can be poor; hiring is a muscle to train.

quote.text: I made a lot of bad hires overseas. It's just like a muscle you have to train hiring.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't say yes to implementation projects you lack capacity for; stick to consulting if that scales better.

lessons.lesson: Start with paying B2B clients rather than consumer apps; client money and feedback tells you what to build.

quote.text: you need to get someone who's going to pay you money to build out features and then like have them use it and get feedback
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

lessons.lesson: Niche B2B tools used by one or two people avoid scale and edge-case complexity, so finishing is easier.
Undercut a recurring-cost alternative with a cheaper custom build and a small monthly fee to win the sale.
Pick one AI stack and become known for it; reuse components and sell customised variants.
AI prototyping lets you scratch shiny-object itches in about 45 minutes instead of weeks, so use time-boxed constraints.

quote.text: now I can like realize an idea in 45 minutes in replet or bolt or whatever
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

lessons.lesson: Focus filter: are people paying or trying to pay me for this? If not, limit time.

quote.text: Money. Are people paying me to do this? Yes or no?
quote.speaker: Billy Howell

lessons.lesson: Prepare distribution assets (landing page, paid calendar) before a viral moment so you can capitalise; years of posting before anything stuck.
Consulting sells decisions made for time-poor people and scales better than building projects.

quote.text: you're selling decisions made for someone who has limited time and resources
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Big SaaS platforms with open APIs may be displaced by cheap custom headless apps built on top.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with a credible process (Upwork, demo-first selling) but almost no revenue figures, client counts or build fees; ideas side-discussed are speculative.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Billy sells app agency services and has a YouTube channel; says he is not sponsored by Replit. Host promotes his own newsletter/podcast.
